sutra.name: Urdhva Tiryagbhyam
sutra.description: The most general and powerful multiplication sutra. It works for multiplying numbers of any length using a criss-cross pattern. This method is often faster than conventional long multiplication.

lessons.title: Two-Digit Multiplication
lessons.description: Multiply two 2-digit numbers mentally using the Vertically and Crosswise method.
lessons.content:
Two-Digit Multiplication

Vertically and Crosswise

Urdhva Tiryagbhyam translates to "Vertically and Crosswise". It is the most general formula applicable to all cases of multiplication. The method uses a criss-cross pattern to compute products efficiently.

The 3-Step Diamond Pattern

For a two-digit multiplication (AB × CD), the process follows these three steps:

  1. Step 1 (Right Vertical - Units column): Multiply the unit digits: B × D.
  2. Step 2 (Crosswise - Diagonal sum): Multiply crosswise and add them: (A × D) + (B × C).
  3. Step 3 (Left Vertical - Tens column): Multiply the tens digits: A × C.

Visual Pattern:

Step 1: |
Step 2: X
Step 3: |

Examples

  • Example 1: 23 × 12 = 276
    Step 1: 3 × 2 = 6
    Step 2: (2 × 2) + (3 × 1) = 4 + 3 = 7
    Step 3: 2 × 1 = 2
    Result: 276
  • Example 2: 47 × 36 = 1692
    Step 1: 7 × 6 = 42 (Write 2, carry 4)
    Step 2: (4 × 6) + (7 × 3) = 24 + 21 = 45. Add carry 4 = 49 (Write 9, carry 4)
    Step 3: 4 × 3 = 12. Add carry 4 = 16
    Result: 1692
  • Example 3: 89 × 94 = 8366
    Step 1: 9 × 4 = 36 (Write 6, carry 3)
    Step 2: (8 × 4) + (9 × 9) = 32 + 81 = 113. Add carry 3 = 116 (Write 6, carry 11)
    Step 3: 8 × 9 = 72. Add carry 11 = 83
    Result: 8366

steps: Step 1 (Vertically Right): 3 × 2 = 6. Q units digit = 6, carry = 0.
Combine parts from left to right: 276.

Step 2 (Crosswise): (4 × 6) + (7 × 3) = 24 + 21 = 45. Add carry 4 = 49. Q tens digit = 9, carry = 4.
Step 3 (Vertically Left): 4 × 3 = 12. Add carry 4 = 16. Q hundreds and thousands digits = 16.
Combine parts from left to right: 1692.

lessons.title: Three-Digit Multiplication
lessons.description: Extend the vertical and crosswise pattern symmetrically to multiply 3-digit numbers in 5 simple steps.
lessons.content:
Three-Digit Multiplication

Extending the Pattern

For 3-digit numbers (ABC × DEF), we extend the vertical and crosswise pattern symmetrically into a 5-step process.

The 5-Step Star Pattern

StepOperation NameFormula
1Right VerticalC × F
2Outer Right Crosswise(B × F) + (C × E)
3Full Star Crosswise + Center Vertical(A × F) + (C × D) + (B × E)
4Outer Left Crosswise(A × E) + (B × D)
5Left VerticalA × D

Asymmetrical Sizing Rule

If you need to multiply a 3-digit number by a 2-digit number (e.g., 524 × 32), simply pad the smaller number with a leading zero (524 × 032) to use the same 3-digit method.

Examples

  • Example 1: 123 × 112 = 13776
    S1: 3 × 2 = 6
    S2: (2 × 2) + (3 × 1) = 4 + 3 = 7
    S3: (1 × 2) + (3 × 1) + (2 × 1) = 2 + 3 + 2 = 7
    S4: (1 × 1) + (2 × 1) = 1 + 2 = 3
    S5: 1 × 1 = 1
    Result: 13776
  • Example 2: 412 × 234 = 96408
    S1: 2 × 4 = 8
    S2: (1 × 4) + (2 × 3) = 4 + 6 = 10 (0, carry 1)
    S3: (4 × 4) + (2 × 2) + (1 × 3) = 16 + 4 + 3 = 23. Add carry 1 = 24 (4, carry 2)
    S4: (4 × 3) + (1 × 2) = 12 + 2 = 14. Add carry 2 = 16 (6, carry 1)
    S5: 4 × 2 = 8. Add carry 1 = 9
    Result: 96408
  • Example 3: 524 × 32 = 16768
    Pad to 524 × 032.
    S1: 4 × 2 = 8
    S2: (2 × 2) + (4 × 3) = 4 + 12 = 16 (6, carry 1)
    S3: (5 × 2) + (4 × 0) + (2 × 3) = 10 + 0 + 6 = 16. Add carry 1 = 17 (7, carry 1)
    S4: (5 × 3) + (2 × 0) = 15 + 0 = 15. Add carry 1 = 16 (6, carry 1)
    S5: 5 × 0 = 0. Add carry 1 = 1
    Result: 16768

steps: S3 (Full Star Crosswise + Center Vertical): (1 × 2) + (3 × 1) + (2 × 1) = 2 + 3 + 2 = 7. (hundreds digit 7)
examples.explanation: A zero-carry 3-digit multiplication showing the 5-step pattern.

lessons.title: Decimal Multiplication
lessons.description: Apply Urdhva Tiryagbhyam to decimals by multiplying as integers first, then placing the decimal point.
lessons.content:
Decimal Multiplication

Applying Urdhva Tiryagbhyam

The Urdhva Tiryagbhyam sutra works perfectly for decimal numbers. The process is straight-forward: ignore the decimal point during multiplication, then place it correctly in the final answer.

  1. Ignore the decimal points first.
  2. Multiply the resulting numbers using the standard 2-digit or 3-digit Urdhva Tiryagbhyam method.
  3. Count the total decimal places in both original numbers.
  4. Place the decimal point from right to left in the final answer.

Examples

  • Example 1: 2.3 × 4.5 = 10.35
    Ignore decimals: 23 × 45 = 1035 (using 2-digit Urdhva Tiryagbhyam).
    Count total decimal places: 1 + 1 = 2.
    Place decimal point 2 places from right: 10.35
  • Example 2: 1.25 × 3.2 = 4.00
    Ignore decimals: 125 × 32 = 4000 (using 3-digit Urdhva Tiryagbhyam on 125 × 032).
    Count total decimal places: 2 + 1 = 3.
    Place decimal point 3 places from right: 4.000 → 4.00

steps: Count total decimal places in original numbers: 1 + 1 = 2.
Place decimal point 2 places from the right: 10.35.
examples.explanation: Multiplying two decimals by treating them as integers first, then placing the decimal point.

steps: Place decimal point 3 places from right: 4.000, which simplifies to 4.00.
examples.explanation: Multiplication with different decimal places, simplified at the end.

lessons.title: Squaring Any Number
lessons.description: Use the general crosswise pattern to square any 2-digit or 3-digit number lightning fast.
lessons.content:
Squaring Any Number

Squaring with Urdhva Tiryagbhyam

Squaring a number AB is the same as multiplying AB × AB using the Urdhva Tiryagbhyam crosswise pattern. It simplifies the generic formula beautifully.

The simplified formula for a 2-digit number AB:

  • RHS: B²
  • Middle: 2 × A × B
  • LHS: A²

Examples

  • Example 1: 23² = 529
    RHS: 3² = 9
    Middle: 2 × 2 × 3 = 12 (write 2, carry 1)
    LHS: 2² = 4 + carry 1 = 5
    Result: 529
  • Example 2: 45² = 2025
    RHS: 5² = 25 (write 5, carry 2)
    Middle: 2 × 4 × 5 = 40. 40 + carry 2 = 42 (write 2, carry 4)
    LHS: 4² = 16. 16 + carry 4 = 20
    Result: 2025
  • Example 3: 123² = 15129
    Treat as 123 × 123 using the full 3-digit method.
    S1: 3² = 9
    S2: 2 × (2 × 3) = 12 (2, carry 1)
    S3: 2 × (1 × 3) + 2² = 6 + 4 = 10. Add carry 1 = 11 (1, carry 1)
    S4: 2 × (1 × 2) = 4. Add carry 1 = 5
    S5: 1² = 1
    Result: 15129

examples.explanation: Squaring a 2-digit number using the specific formula derived from Urdhva Tiryagbhyam.

steps: Treat as 123 × 123 using the full 3-digit method.
examples.explanation: Squaring a 3-digit number by simplifying the symmetric crosswise pattern.
